From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@helix.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixAI pilot: Redwood-verified perf pack, prompts, and next steps

Hi Jessica — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Recap from discovery
- Goal: Add an assistant to Helix Studio to handle developer troubleshooting and code snippet generation with high fidelity (technical domain).
- Target latency: p95 < 250ms for short dev completions (<= 128 tokens).
- Throughput requirement: sustained ~120 QPS during business hours; spikes to 300 QPS tolerated for short windows.
- SLOs: budget-sensitive; prefer a solution that trades some cost for predictable p95s and no regressions on accuracy for safety-critical snippets.

Redwood recommendations (shortlist for pilot)
1) Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized) — best cost/quality for short developer completions; expect ~210ms p95 at 128 tokens on T4-equivalent nodes.
2) Llama-2-13B-Chat (q4) — higher quality on complex reasoning prompts; expect ~320ms p95 but better correctness on multi-step code tasks.
3) Redstone-34B (fp16) — top-quality variant for hardest reasoning; reserve for canary/edge cases due to cost.

What I attached
- helix_prompt_set_v1.txt: your canonical prompt templates + a 60-example evaluation set (anonymized).
- redwood_perf_pack_v3.pdf: Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS baselines, latency percentiles, memory footprints) and recommended serving configs.

Quick notes about perf numbers in the pack (high level)
- TPS is measured on our continuous-batching runtime; numbers assume a pinned model variant and the sequence length distribution in the attached prompts.
- Example: Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4) => 140 TPS per 8-GPU pod, p50=62ms, p95=210ms, p99=410ms for 128-token requests.

Proposed pilot plan (2 weeks)
- Week 1: Redwood runs the benchmark harness against your 60-example eval; collect throughput/latency + quality (exact-match & human-rated)
- Week 2: Helix runs a shadow traffic experiment for 48h (non-prod traffic) + we run an A/B of Llama-13B vs Mistral w/ your prompts.
- Deliverables: Bench report, suggested model + quantization profile, cost estimate for production, checklist for rollout.

Open questions / asks for you
- Can you share a 24h representative traffic sample (anonymized)? We included a small sample in the prompt set but need broader distribution.
- Any security constraints we should account for (SSO, IP allowlist, data retention window)?

Next steps
- If that plan works, propose we kick off Friday 19 Mar (prep) and start runs Mon 22 Mar.
- Please confirm who on your side will own the shadow-run coordination and procurement touchpoints.

Thanks — looping in Ava and Dev to scope the benchmark harness and infra.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: helix_prompt_set_v1.txt, redwood_perf_pack_v3.pdf

Thanks Jessica — noted on ownership (appreciate you taking ops). A few follow-ups from our side: 

1) Cost ballpark for 2-week pilot (estimate)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4, dedicated 8-GPU pod during runs): ~$3.2k — $4.5k depending on runtime hours and burst windows.
- Llama-2-13B (q4): ~$6k — $8.5k (higher compute).
- Redstone-34B (fp16): reserve-only; expect 3x-4x cost of 13B variant.

2) On SOW / legal templates: I'll have our legal team push a pilot SOW + confidentiality addendum; can send a draft by EOD Wed 17 Mar.

3) Prep asks for the benchmark run (what Ava & Dev need)
- Full 24h anonymized traffic sample (link to Drive or S3). If you can upload a 1% sample to the Drive link in the related_links field that will work.
- A short list of failure modes you especially care about (e.g., hallucination on code blocks, conditional license text).
- Confirmation on retention: recommended default for pilot is 30 days for logs + metrics; let us know if you need shorter.

4) Quality/regression concern: Our baseline evaluation includes an exact-match + human-rated pass/fail. We flagged two categories that often regress across quantization: tokenization-sensitive code snippets (inline code blocks) and long-context stateful threads. If those are high-risk we should keep the 13B variant in the A/B for a longer window.

Looping Ava and Dev — Ava, can you confirm you have capacity to run the benchmark harness Mon/Tue next week and whether you need a specific infra profile?

— Logan

Thanks — tagging in technical details and what we'll deliver for the benchmark harness.

What we'll run
- Redwood eval harness (v2.8): exact-match, BLEU-ish code similarity, and a 5-rater human review for a 60-example subset.
- Perf harness: synthetic concurrency sweep (1 -> 400 concurrent sessions) using your 24h histogram to drive sequence-length distributions.

Infra profile we need from Helix
- A 1% anonymized payload dump (sample_payloads_anon.jsonl) uploaded to the Drive link in related_links. Prefer JSONL with fields: request_id, prompt, seq_len, metadata (no PII).
- IP allowlist entries for our runner and temporary service account.
- Point of contact for troubleshooting: Jessica (ops) is fine; include a senior infra engineer if possible.

Regression guardrails we will enforce
- Tokenization-sensitivity check: we will run the prompt set through each quantized runtime and highlight any exact-match drops > 8%.
- Long-context drift check: for prompts flagged as stateful, we'll measure consistency across 3 repeated runs.

Deliverables and timing
- Thu 18 Mar EOD: confirmation that sample payloads are uploaded.
- Fri 19 Mar: bench harness prep complete; legal SOW draft review.
- Mon 22 Mar: start perf + quality runs. Initial interim report by Wed 24 Mar.

Let me know if Helix has any constraints on human review (NDA / access). Otherwise we'll proceed with our standard 5-rater anonymized workflow.

— Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
